text: That history of alcohol use and acute abdominal pain is concerning. Has this pain been in your right upper abdomen, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs or abdominal distension recently? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Bilirubin_Total 5.6 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 192 U/L, AST 32 U/L, ALT 34 U/L. Abdominal_Ultrasound: Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region. Dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a cystic mass compressing the bile ducts, which explains the obstruction. Was there any history of trauma or surgery in that area, and does the mass feel mobile or fixed during palpation? REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant for detailed anatomical assessment.

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Extrahepatic Cholestasis due to Choledochal Cyst. The combination of a cystic mass in the subhepatic region causing biliary obstruction, along with significant weight loss and a smoking history, is highly suggestive of this congenital anomaly. Given the patient's age and symptoms, I recommend further imaging to rule out malignancy such as cholangiocarcinoma or pancreatic head cancer.
